title: Biodegradable Polymer Synthesis
keywords_for_the_page_and_card: Materials chemistry · Chitin · Marine degradation · Circular materials
intro: Most plastics that reach the sea stay there. We design materials that do not — and measure how quickly they disappear.

add_image.image_alt: Biodegradable polymer samples on a laboratory bench

add_focus_list: Chitin and chitosan films from shellfish waste
Seawater degradation measured under controlled conditions
Mechanical properties tuned for packaging and coatings
Life-cycle assessment with regional waste streams
add_paragraph:
Chitin is the second most abundant biopolymer on Earth and a large fraction of it is discarded by the seafood industry. We turn that waste into films and coatings whose degradation rate can be tuned — fast enough to disappear in seawater, slow enough to do their job on a shelf.

Every formulation is tested in the same seawater mesocosm, with mass loss, oxygen demand and fragmentation tracked over twelve months. The results feed a simple question: is this material genuinely better, or just differently labelled?

images.image_caption: From shellfish waste to compostable film.
